## Description

Add a `perf` package with a span-based API (inspired by OpenTelemetry) for measuring per-step latency inside git hooks. Root spans should emit a single structured DEBUG log line on completion with the hook name, `duration_ms` and per-step `steps.<name>_ms` keys. Partio writes its log only to stderr (`internal/log/log.go`), so a user sees the timing line in the terminal when a hook runs at the debug level, for example `PARTIO_LOG_LEVEL=debug git commit`.

In `post-commit` (`internal/hooks/postcommit.go`) the steps are: reading the pre-commit state, `attribution.Calculate`, `FindLatestSession`, `git.AmendTrailers` and `store.Write`. The existing `slog.Debug("checkpoint created", ...)` line is where the post-commit timings can go. #290 asked for the same timing in `post-commit` only.

#352 (merged here) adds four outputs to the debug line:

- Write the last run of each hook to `.partio/state/hook-timing.json`, for example `{"hook": "post-commit", "phases": [{"name": "FindLatestSession", "duration_ms": 42}], "total_ms": 350}`. Each run overwrites the file.
- Add `hook_warn_threshold_ms` to the config (default `5000`). When the total of a hook is more than this value, log one WARN line. The default level is `info` (`internal/config/defaults.go`), so the warning shows without debug.
- `partio doctor` prints the timings of the last hook run from `hook-timing.json`.
- `partio status --verbose` prints the total duration of the last hook run. #345 adds the same flag for the hook phase: the issue that is built first adds the flag.

Use one list of step names for this issue, #217 (live progress) and #345 (phase in status).

## Why

Git hook latency directly impacts developer experience — every `git commit` blocks on hooks. Without per-step breakdown, diagnosing bottlenecks requires code changes rather than log inspection. This enables users and support to quickly identify which step is slow.

## Source

- **Origin:** entireio/cli#614, entireio/cli#652
- **Detected from:** `entireio-cli-pulls`

## Target Repos

- `cli`
- `docs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each hook invocation (`pre-commit`, `post-commit`, `pre-push`) emits a single DEBUG log line to stderr with the hook name, `duration_ms` and the per-step breakdown when `PARTIO_LOG_LEVEL=debug` (the level match in `internal/log/log.go` is case-sensitive)
- [ ] Each hook run writes its step timings to `.partio/state/hook-timing.json` and overwrites the last run
- [ ] A hook whose total is more than `hook_warn_threshold_ms` (default 5000) logs one WARN line
- [ ] `partio doctor` shows the timings of the last hook run
- [ ] `partio status --verbose` shows the total duration of the last hook run
- [ ] Unit tests cover span creation, nesting, duration recording, error recording, and idempotent End()
- [ ] Docs describe how to read the hook timings with `PARTIO_LOG_LEVEL=debug`
